blocks.text: Brackenridge Civil Group Inc is a small civil engineering practice in the county seat, and it has kept to the same steady work since it was founded in 1996. We design the grading, drainage, roadway, and utility improvements a site needs before it can be built. Our clients are the public bodies and private builders who work here: municipal public works departments, a regional water authority, and private developers. The firm has stayed deliberately small, close to its work and its records, and this overview describes what it does and shows the work through two representative engagements. It is written to claim only what is true.

A civil design touches the ground and everything set into it, and the firm's lines of work follow from that. We grade sites so they sit and drain as they must, and we design the erosion and sediment control that holds the soil while it is disturbed. We design stormwater management, from the drainage study that stands behind a plan through the pipes, inlets, and detention that carry runoff off a site within the county's standards. We lay out roadways, whether a new street or the widening and resurfacing of an old one, and we design the water, sanitary sewer, and storm utilities that run beneath them. On a subdivision these arrive as one coordinated set. On a public works job they may come one line at a time, as the county's program and budget allow. The small job has the same claim on our care as the large one.

The firm holds to a plain order of work, and it does not vary it. A job begins with a walk of the site and a scope set down in writing, so the client and the firm agree on the work before it starts. The design is done at our own boards and checked before it is issued. Nothing leaves this office until the set has been reviewed and the cover sheet sealed. The construction documents we prepare, the drawings and the specifications, are made to be built from and to carry a contractor and a reviewer through the work without guesswork. The practice is small enough that the same hand reaches every job and steady enough to keep several moving at once.

A good part of the firm's work is done for public agencies, and it is prepared to their standards and their review. We take a set through the county's drainage and roadway review, prepare the permit documents a job requires, and answer the comments that come back until the set is approved. The paperwork is kept as carefully as the drawings, so that a project folder holds the whole record of a job. Public work runs on that kind of order, and the firm is built for it.

Two projects, a few years apart, give a fair sense of the work. On the earlier of them, for {{fact:f:E-2001-001.client}}, we carried the site grading and stormwater design from the first walk of the ground through the county's review. More recently, for {{fact:f:E-2004-001.client}}, we handled the roadway and utility design and saw the set through approval. We offer these as examples of the kind of project the firm takes on, not as a list of our clients or a measure of the firm's work, and we do not, as a matter of practice, discuss one client's engagement with another.

If you have a project that needs civil design, begin with a conversation. Direct inquiries to Mark Todd, Principal Engineer, who will walk the site and set a scope in writing before any work is undertaken.
